questions.question: In Tolman's maze learning experiment the fact that the group of rats receiving reinforcement only after the 10th day of the study solved the maze far more quickly than did the rats who had been reinforced from the first day can be interpreted to mean that these particular rats:
options: (A) were much more intelligent than the other rats
(B) had already learnt the maze in the first nine days
(C) had the opportunity to cheat by watching the other rats
(D) were very hungry and therefore learned much more quickly
questions.correct_text: had already learnt the maze in the first nine days
questions.concept: Tolman's latent learning — learning occurs without reinforcement, demonstrated when reward is introduced

questions.question: Who added the concept of reinforcement to learning theory?
questions.concept: Thorndike's Law of Effect — added reinforcement concept through satisfaction/stamp-in

questions.question: What type of memory allows us to have meaningful conversation?
questions.concept: STM/Working memory enables holding and processing information for conversations

questions.question: When Mohan studies Psychological terms, he tries to tie each concept into something he already knows. He thinks about the meaning of the concept rather than just saying the words over and over. Which model of memory would best explain Mohan's approach to encoding memories?
questions.concept: Craik & Lockhart's Levels of Processing — deep/semantic processing leads to better retention

questions.question: The best place to take your psychology exam to ensure good retrieval of psychological concept is in the
options: (D) Special testing room used for all exams
questions.concept: Context-dependent memory (Godden & Baddeley) — best retrieval in same context as encoding

questions.question: Which one of the following statement about type 'A' individual is not correct?
questions.concept: Type A personality: competitive, aggressive, impatient, time-pressured, hostile — not characterized as sociable

questions.question: Trait Approach to personality asserts that traits are
options: (B) Discrete and discontinuous categories of people
(C) Generalized system which ensure consistency in behaviour of individual
(D) Psychological categories of Temperament associated with specific body physique
questions.correct_text: Generalized system which ensure consistency in behaviour of individual
questions.concept: Trait approach (Allport, Cattell, Eysenck) — traits are stable, generalized neuropsychic structures/dispositions that initiate and guide consistent forms of adaptive and expressive behavior across situations

questions.question: Which one of the following statement indicates true relation between intelligence and creativity?
options: (A) Intelligence and creativity have high correlation
(B) Intelligence and creativity have low correlation
(C) Intelligence and creativity have moderate correlation
(D) Intelligence and creativity have higher correlation at the lower level than at higher level of intelligence
questions.correct_text: Intelligence and creativity have higher correlation at the lower level than at higher level of intelligence
questions.concept: Threshold theory — higher IQ-creativity correlation below IQ ~120; above threshold, correlation weakens

questions.question: A psychological test can be considered as standard when one establishes its
questions.concept: Standardized test requires reliability, validity, and established norms

questions.question: Parallel lines such as Railway Track appear to converge on a distant-point called vanishing point. This phenomenon is explained by the principle of
questions.concept: Linear perspective — parallel lines appear to converge at vanishing point

questions.question: Dark adaptation is a process in which eyes get more sensitive to
questions.concept: Dark adaptation — increased sensitivity to dim light through rod activation

questions.question: Which of the following statement explains incidental learning?
options: (A) learning without actually trying to attain a goal
(B) learning in absence of ostensible reinforcement
(C) learning without knowledge of relationship between response and reinforcement
(D) learning in absence of changes in perception or discrimination
questions.correct_text: learning without actually trying to attain a goal
questions.concept: Incidental learning — learning that occurs without deliberate intention

questions.question: Which one of the following factor is not included in big five dimensions of personality?
questions.concept: Big Five (OCEAN): Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism — dominance not included

questions.question: Secret of coping with stress is to be willing to modify our construct to fit into the new situation. This statement is attributed to
questions.concept: Kelly's Personal Construct Theory — modifying constructs to fit new situations as coping

questions.question: An emotion is best defined as
options: (C) An excited state arising in response to stimuli for which the individual doesn't have adequate readymade reactions
(D) Display excessive or irrational behaviour as a result of unexpected or intense stimuli
questions.correct_text: An excited state arising in response to stimuli for which the individual doesn't have adequate readymade reactions
questions.concept: McDougall's definition — emotion is an excited state when the individual lacks adequate readymade (instinctive) reactions to stimuli; emotion serves as a motivational signal for novel situations

questions.question: Which one of the following statement regarding field experiment is not true?
options: (A) Field experiments require investigators who are specially skilled for intervening in social situation
(B) The greatest difficulty in field experiment lies in the randomization and manipulation of the independent variable
(C) Field experiments are concerned with causal relationship but not with the direction of relationship
(D) Field experiments are carried out in natural setting
questions.correct_text: Field experiments are concerned with causal relationship but not with the direction of relationship
questions.concept: Field experiments CAN establish direction of relationship; they are concerned with both causation and direction

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is/are correct regarding perception?

(i) Perception is not directly observable.
(ii) Perception is followed by sensation.
(iii) Perception can be modified.
(iv) Perception is inherited.

Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.concept: Perception is not directly observable (i) and can be modified through learning (iii); sensation precedes perception (ii is wrong)

questions.question: The memory trace if not revived from time gradually fades out according to law of disuse until it is completely obliterated. It is called
questions.concept: Anti-consolidation / Trace decay theory — memory traces gradually fade if not revived (Thorndike's law of disuse); absence of consolidation prevents long-term stabilization of the memory trace, leading to eventual obliteration

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** According to Freud, all behaviours stemmed from two opposing groups of instincts.

**Reason (R):** Some instincts are innate and some are acquired.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Freud's two groups of instincts (Eros and Thanatos); all instincts are innate in Freud's theory

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** People in cinema hall can be readily grouped into high, middle and low income categories.

**Reason (R):** Perceptual grouping may be done on the principle of proximity and similarity.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Income grouping via cinema seating is social/economic categorization; Gestalt proximity/similarity are true perceptual principles but do not explain income-based grouping

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** A forty year old man may have the same IQ as that of a 20 year old.

**Reason (R):** The forty year old man could have been somewhat retarded to start with.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Deviation IQ can be same across ages; retardation is not the explanation — IQ is relative to age norms

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Any psychological or physiological imbalance motivates behaviour.

**Reason (R):** The body tends to maintain internal balance.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Drive-reduction theory and homeostasis — imbalance creates drive; body seeks internal balance

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** In proactive inhibition, early learning interferes with later learning.

**Reason (R):** If a person goes to sleep immediately after learning, forgetting will be less.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Proactive interference defined correctly; sleep reduces retroactive interference (not proactive); both true but R doesn't explain A

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Performance of a person is a function of his motivational level.

**Reason (R):** There is a linear relationship between arousal and performance.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Performance relates to motivation (A is true); arousal-performance is curvilinear (inverted-U), not linear

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Eidetic imagery is rare in adults.

**Reason (R):** The loss in eidetic imagery may be related to the development of Abstract Thinking.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Eidetic imagery (photographic memory) rare in adults; development of abstract thinking may cause its decline

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Out of the five correlation coefficients, –0.80, 0.70, 0.50, 0.00, and –0.20, between X and Y variable, the strongest relationship is indicated by a correlation coefficient of 0.70.

**Reason (R):** The correlation coefficient of 0.70 indicates that X increases, Y also tends to increase.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Strongest correlation is -0.80 (not 0.70) as strength is measured by absolute value; 0.70 does show positive relationship

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Limbic system is a group of structures in the cardiovascular region.

**Reason (R):** Limbic system is involved in expression of emotion and motivation.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Limbic system is in the brain (not cardiovascular); involved in emotion and motivation

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Neither trait nor type theory can explain total personality.

**Reason (R):** Personality is the interactive product of individuality and environment.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.correct_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.concept: Trait theories (Allport, Cattell, Eysenck) describe stable dispositions but neglect situational variability; type theories (Sheldon, Kretschmer) categorize into discrete groups oversimplifying complexity. Neither can explain total personality because personality emerges from the dynamic reciprocal interplay of individual (biological, cognitive, dispositional) and environmental (social, cultural, situational) factors — a limitation addressed by interactionist (Bandura's reciprocal determinism) and social-cognitive approaches

questions.question: The Theories of Intelligence appeared in the following order. Select the correct order:
questions.concept: Chronological order: Binet-Simon scale (1905, first practical intelligence test) → Spearman's two-factor/g-factor theory (1904 paper, 1927 comprehensive work) → Thurstone's Primary Mental Abilities (1938) → Cattell's fluid-crystallized intelligence (1963). In UGC NET context, Binet-Simon is placed first as the initiator of intelligence measurement

questions.concept: Gestalt psychologists chronological order: Wertheimer (1912) → Koffka → Kohler → Lewin

questions.question: Piaget suggested the following development stages. Which one is correct?
options: (A) Sensori-motor / Concrete operations / Pre-operational / Formal operational
(B) Sensori-motor, Pre-operational, Concrete operations, Formal operational
(C) Sensori motor / Pre-operational / Formal operational / Concrete operations
(D) Concrete operations / Sensori motor / Formal operational / Pre-operational
questions.correct_text: Sensori-motor, Pre-operational, Concrete operations, Formal operational
questions.concept: Piaget's four stages of cognitive development in correct order: (1) Sensorimotor stage (birth to 2 years) - knowledge through sensory experiences and motor actions; (2) Pre-operational stage (2 to 7 years) - symbolic thinking but lacks logical operations; (3) Concrete operational stage (7 to 11 years) - logical thinking about concrete events; (4) Formal operational stage (11 years and above) - abstract and hypothetical thinking. Option (B) correctly presents this sequential order.

questions.concept: Bandura's observational learning sequence: Attention → Retention → Reproduction → Motivation

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of steps involving creative thinking?
questions.concept: Wallas's (1926) four stages of creative thinking in correct order: (1) Preparation - defining the problem and gathering information systematically; (2) Incubation - unconscious processing where the problem is set aside; (3) Illumination - the 'Eureka moment' of sudden insight when the solution emerges; (4) Verification - testing and validating the solution. Option (A) correctly presents this sequential order.

content.heading: Stress is a state of tension that occurs when there are demands and pressures that tax an individual's ability to adjust.
content.text:
Stress is a state of tension that occurs when there are demands and pressures that tax an individual's ability to adjust. Stress typically results from the challenge of adjusting to transitions in life, and college is a time of significant change. Any disease, including hypertension, heart disease, ulcers and diabetes, have been found to have a strong correlation with stress. In addition, stress may aggravate or even be a causal factor in other conditions, such as headache, backache, skin disorders, indigestion, respiratory ailments, mental illness and accidental injuries. Stress in college can result from external sources such as academic demands or relationship conflicts, or from internally generated expectations for self. The stress response is very personal and varies for different students.

Every one working at university has contact with students. Sadly, many students experience severe psychological problems that may go unnoticed or ignored until it is too late. College students often face depression, anxiety relationship difficulties and feelings of isolation fear of failure, family pressures, and "difficulty in adjusting". Without help, the pressure may build until it becomes a crisis situation (severe depression, suicidal thoughts and / or attempts, panic attacks etc). A psychological crisis situation occurs when the student feels unable to cope with the circumstances of his/her life. The more helpless the individual feels, the greater the crisis.

A student's support system (including family friends, acquaintances etc) is critical. More extensive the support system, the better the prognosis of the student. Both psychological crisis and emergencies warrant an immediate call to the Student Health Center for crisis intervention.

Crisis intervention, thus helps a person cope with the immediate situation and make a plan to address any ongoing problems. Qualified mental health professional can help people address the causes of their distress and teach them effective ways to deal with those causes. Every detection and treatment can head off serious consequences.

questions.question: Physical diseases such as heart disease, hypertension, ulcers and diabetes tend to have:

questions.correct_text: He is better able to lessen the impact of Psychological Crisis and emergencies
questions.concept: Social support as protective factor — lessens psychological crisis impact
